title: Morton session personnel, trumpets and the trio sides
summary: Talk of Stump Evans, Shirley Clay, the Dodds trio sides, multiple masters and how loose the written ensembles were.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Stump Evans was in that -- on that recording date. Alto player?
Yeah.
Was his name Stump or Stomp? I've seen it both ways.
Now, you know, I don't remember. Because we always called him Stump.
Stump?
Yeah.
Sometimes he's referred to as Stomp Evans.
Yeah. I've heard Stump.
Stump, was he a short man, or --
Yeah. Yeah, he was short.
The ensembles on these records, I was listening to them again last night. Parts of it sound like there are two trumpets. Was there just the one trumpet?
It could have been, what's the name,
Clay?
Shirley Clay?
Shirley Clay, and Joyce could have been on the record.
Uh-huh. Why do you say they could have been?
You say it sound like two trumpets.
Yeah. But why do you say Shirley Clay might have been?
Because I know he made some of the sessions with us.
He made some of the sessions with you?
Yeah, he, Shirley Clay, yeah.
And Jelly?
Yeah.
One of the sessions the band -- the session that you recorded "The Pearls," according to the discographies, that was the same date that Jelly made a couple of trio sides with Johnny and Baby Dodds?
Uh-huh.
Were you there when they made that?
Yeah, I was there.
I mean, did he just say, I want to do this trio thing?
Yeah.
And there are a couple of different masters available of that. And also of "Pearls" I believe. "Pearls" has two masters.
Yeah?
Yeah, there's two of "Beale Street," and there's two of the "Pearls", and two of "Wolverine Blues." That have been issued.
Yeah?

These are French records. And there's some variation, you know, on the solos and in the ensembles. It seems like some of the arrangements had loose parts in them, you know, where you didn't have to do exactly what Jelly had written or instructed you to do. Am I wrong there, or was it all very strictly controlled?
Well, except for the solos. You know, you did your own improvising on your solos.
The ensembles sound very loose, you know, these New Orleans ensembles.
Yeah, that's the way he wrote.
Did the guys have trouble reading it?
No.
